$meta.name: openDash design tokens
$meta.note: Single source of truth. Feeds (a) the .djson generator, (b) the plugin settings panel, (c) the design canvas under design/canvas. Never hand-edit colours downstream. A token carrying a scope is not expressible on the dash face.
$meta.layers: Three layers. palette: raw scales, never used directly. semantic: what a colour means (a state, a surface, a text role), with primary, secondary and tint shades. purpose: what a colour is for on a given element (delta.slower, lap.sessionBest, flag.blue), always an alias into semantic. A value written as {path} is an alias into another token.
$meta.parts: The same layering applies to the parts. element: label, numeral, rule, segment, band. component: readout, grid, revBar, one component per flag, pitLimiter, popUp, listRow. page: a changeable module a zone shows, from its own catalogue. zone: a named region of a face that cycles its catalogue from a wheel button. layout: a screen size that fixes the five parts' rectangles. See docs/design/zones.md.

changelog.0.9.2: font.cell records the monospace cells a value is drawn in, and rule 19 says what may go in one.
changelog.0.9.1: Rule 18: every drawing is cut from its box rather than placed in it at a fixed size.
changelog.0.9.0: The shape model: a page is laid out for the shape of its zone rather than its width, and every page has a version for every shape a real face gives it.
changelog.0.8.0: The telltales, and the icon library behind them.
changelog.0.7.0: The drawings lost their fills and the fuel tank was dropped: a drawing on the face needs no tray under it and a quantity is a number. Band D became a centred rank with a corner block at each end, and a zone narrow enough for one column centres what is in it.
changelog.0.6.0: The slot and cell models were replaced by the zone model: a bar of settled values, zones A, B and C, band D, and a catalogue and a button per zone. card.span stays only as a record of the pass it supersedes.
changelog.0.4.0: purpose.licence, purpose.rating, purpose.block and purpose.illustration, with metrics for block, badge, flagIcon and each drawn object.
changelog.0.3.0: The palette, semantic and purpose layers.

palette.note: 200 is the working shade, the only one that appears on the dash face. 100 is a tint for hover and highlight in the plugin and on monitors. 300 is a dark shade for fills behind text on the pit wall and for muted marks. Both were derived from 200 at equal chroma; nothing else on the face uses them.

base.desc: Dash background and plugin panel. Near-black, not pure black: pure black blooms on OLED/IPS DDUs.

zone.desc: Zone fill on the dash; list row and input fill in the plugin.

raised.desc: Separator rules on both surfaces; hover fill in the plugin.

dim.desc: Inactive segment, missing data, control outline.

caution.desc: Caution, shift stage 2, an update waiting.

danger.desc: Alarm, slower, shift stage 3, a failure.

best.desc: Session best. Sim racing purple convention.

brand.desc: openDash identity ONLY: logo, plugin panel, docs. NEVER appears on the dash face, so it can never be misread as a state.

yellow.desc: Yellow flag. Flag yellow is not caution amber, on purpose: the two sit side by side on a yellow-flag lap.

black.desc: Drawn as an outlined band, since a black band on a near-black face is invisible.

onFlag.desc: Label colour on a flag band.

debris.desc: Yellow band with danger stripes, a pattern like the chequer.

ui.scope: Plugin panel and documentation only. The pit wall and the companion are SimHub dashboards and stay achromatic like the dash face. Where SimHub's own control styles apply (SHButtonPrimary, SHToggleButton, section titles), these override only what those styles leave open.

penalty.desc: Stop and go, drive through, time penalty, disqualification.

power.desc: Engine off, ignition off; drawn outlined.

p2p.desc: Push to pass and headlight flash.

trend.note: A change of setting is information, not a state.

class.note: Class identity is a labelled chip, never a colour, so that second screens stay achromatic. Aliasing the 300 shades here is the option if class colour is ever wanted.

licence.note: An ordered ramp, not a categorical palette. One could think a licence should wear iRacing's own colours, since drivers know them; in reality every one of those five steps is a state colour here, and a green B licence beside a green delta is precisely the confusion the first rule exists to prevent. The class is ordered, so it is drawn as an ordered weight: R is the lightest mark on the screen and Pro the heaviest, and the last two invert exactly as the player's own class chip does.

pro.note: Inverted: dark ink on a light block, as the player's own chip is.

rating.note: A rating is data and stays achromatic. What the race has done to it is an event, so the gain or loss takes a state colour and a drawn triangle, the same mark a position change uses.

fill.note: A fill groups values the eye takes in as one instrument. Four tyre corners are one reading, so they sit on one ground. A card holding one value keeps no fill at all, which is why most of the face is bare.

well.note: Recessed ground behind a gauge or a drawing. The rev bar has sat in one since the first token file named it; it was simply never drawn.

rule.note: A rule, not a box. It is the whole boundary where a block would be too much, and it is what bounds a nationality flag so a white field does not bleed into the page.

block.note: When a fill is allowed. Not under a drawing: a drawing on the face needs no tray, which is why the tyre and the fuel illustrations lost theirs at 0.7.0.

illustration.note: The drawn objects: the tyre, the brake disc, the car and the steering. An object takes the shape of the object -- a tyre has shoulders, a disc is round -- whereas chrome stays square, and an object is only drawn where its shape says something a number does not. That is why fuel is a number and the tank was dropped at 0.7.0. Rule 18: a drawing is cut from its box, never placed in it at a fixed size.

neutral.note: A lamp the standard leaves uncoloured.

off.note: Unlit, and drawn rather than hidden: a lamp coming on is a change of colour and not a change of layout.

telltale.note: The one place on the face where colour is conventional rather than chosen. ISO 2575 fixes the pictogram and its colour and every driver already knows both, so this sits inside the first rule rather than beside it. The pictograms are Material Design Icons by Pictogrammers under the Apache Licence 2.0, taken unmodified and filled, where a user-interface icon is stroked.

data.note: Barlow Condensed, renamed. WPF reads the width out of a family name, folds the condensed faces into Barlow as a stretch, and a .djson can only ask for a family and a weight, so a request for Barlow Condensed reached a face a fifth too wide. The bundled files are renamed on the way into a package, by packages/dash/src/design/fontFiles.ts, and the vendored originals are untouched. The OFL permits it: Barlow declares no Reserved Font Name, the licence ships in fonts/OFL.txt, and the copyright inside each file still credits the Barlow authors.
data.desc: All numerals. DIN-adjacent condensed grotesque. Tabular digits to be verified in the spike.

cell.desc: Monospace cell widths as a fraction of the font size. A ticking value jitters because the digits are proportional, and SimHub exposes no OpenType features, so a value is drawn with SimHub's UseMonospacedText and every character is laid in a cell. Measured from the bundled TTFs to hold the widest ink a value can draw, which lands within one percent of the tabular advance the font itself carries: 0.475 em in SemiBold, 0.498 in Bold. These hold only while the renderer draws the face the design asks for, which for a year it did not: WPF resolved Barlow rather than Barlow Condensed, and a Barlow SemiBold 4 is 0.585 em, a quarter over the cell. Renaming the bundled family settled that resolution, so the cells are the condensed face's own again.

gear.desc: The gear draws N and R as well as digits, and N is the widest of them at 0.514 em in Bold, wider than the widest digit, so the gear cannot use the face's digit cell. 0.52 em is 135 px at 260. It was briefly 0.68 to survive WPF resolving Barlow instead of the condensed face; renaming the family fixed the resolution, so it is back to what the face itself needs.

specialChars.desc: Characters given the narrow cell. A minus keeps the digit cell so a signed value stays in column.

excluded.desc: Characters whose ink overruns the digit cell and which a monospaced value therefore may not contain. A car number is drawn bare and its hash belongs to the label; a composite such as a class and a number is split into a proportional label and a monospaced value.

gearSm.desc: Gear on faces shorter than 300 px of slot region (nano).

value.desc: Card value at rung M, denominator at rung L.

valueSm.desc: Card value at rung S, grid cells at M and S, list rows.

numeralLg.desc: Pit wall table rows and companion lists.

ui.scope: Plugin panel, and the pit wall tables, at 96 dpi logical pixels.

tracking.scope: plugin panel and documentation only. SimHub text items have no letter-spacing property, so tracking cannot be applied on the dash face.

sm.desc: Plugin controls and the segment mark beside the wordmark.

icon.desc: 16 in controls, 20 alone. Stroke 1.5, square caps, mitre joins.

control.scope: Plugin panel. Where SimHub's control styles apply, these describe the openDash-owned controls only.

segments.desc: Settled on the design canvas: 15 segments, radius seg, gap 8 at 1920, 6 at 1280, 4 at 850 and below.

height.desc: 32 on faces 400 px tall or shorter.

shiftLights.stagesNote: Band boundaries are SimHub's per-car values, tuned by the user in SimHub's Car Settings page, never fixed percentages. The whole shift-light layer is hidden when the OpenDash.ShiftLights property is false.

flashHz.desc: Maps to BlinkDelay in milliseconds; verify in the spike that SimHub honours 62 ms.

flagBand.desc: Full-width band at the bottom edge, one flag at a time in scope priority order. Absent, not grey, when no flag is out. On round faces the outer ring takes the flag colour instead.

pitLimiter.desc: Neutral block above the gear, blinking.

popUp.desc: Centred over the hero, one at a time. Post-MVP.

alert.desc: Highest priority active alert, one at a time, in the three flag formats.

header.desc: Companion header keeps position and lap in view; pit wall header carries session, flag, incidents, track state, wind and clocks.

card.note: Every card fits every slot of its layout. A card picks its rung from the slot width, never from its own content. A card that needs more room is two cards.

future.desc: 5in Vocore and round faces with a cover. DNR Chrono. Same layout as 850 with 25 px less per side.
4 to 6.8in wheel and dash screens. DNR Endurance.
Round and square DDUs. Lovely Round and Square.

future.grid: one module at a time behind a header
future.desc: Companion on a wheel or phone. Lovely Companion, DNR Co-Pilot.

future.grid: one module at a time behind a header

future.desc: Secondary monitor, three pages. DNR Race Control, Lovely Pit Wall.
future.zones: up to four data zones per page, eleven standard pages and six wide pages

future.desc: Portrait monitor or tablet. Lovely Pit Wall Portrait.
future.zones: up to four data zones per page, eleven standard pages and six wide pages

screen.note: Every layout declares its own slot count; the plugin exposes slot settings up to the largest count declared.
